cues.en: Instructor: Now that you have a basic grasp of correlation and also covariance and the formula for correlation, testing for statistical significance, and so on,
cues.zh: 講師：你現在對相關、共變異數、相關公式，以及統計顯著性檢定等等，已經有基本掌握，

cues.en: it's time to start learning more advanced topics in correlation analysis.
cues.zh: 接著該開始學習相關分析的進階主題。

cues.en: And we're going to start that by discussing partial correlations.
cues.zh: 我們先從偏相關談起。

cues.en: That's the topic of this video.
cues.zh: 這就是這支影片的主題。

cues.en: So I will explain what partial correlations are, why we need them, and how it works.
cues.zh: 我會說明偏相關是什麼、為什麼需要，以及它如何運作。

cues.en: So here is a system.
cues.zh: 這裡有一個系統。

cues.en: We have a multivariate dataset with three variables.
cues.zh: 是一份有三個變數的多變量資料集。

cues.en: So variable 1, variable 2, and variable 3.
cues.zh: 變數 1、變數 2 與變數 3。

cues.en: And here are the correlations between them.
cues.zh: 這是它們之間的相關。

cues.en: So the correlation between variable 1 and variable 3 is .5.
cues.zh: 變數 1 與變數 3 的相關是 0.5。

cues.en: You can see how I'm showing the correlations between the two variables here in subscripts.
cues.zh: 可以看到，我用下標標示是哪兩個變數之間的相關。

cues.en: Now, there is a potential problem with these correlations, this system of correlations here, and that is that any one of these correlations
cues.zh: 這組相關可能有一個問題，也就是其中任何一個相關，

cues.en: might be artificially or artifactually enhanced, inflated, by the positive correlations between other variables.
cues.zh: 都可能因為其他變數之間的正相關，而被人為或假象地增強、膨脹。

cues.en: So let me attach some labels to this to make it a little bit more sensible.
cues.zh: 替它加上一些標籤，讓意思更清楚。

cues.en: You might remember that at the end of the first video of this section, I was talking about correlation and causation.
cues.zh: 你可能記得，本單元第一支影片結尾，我談到相關與因果。

cues.en: And I gave this funny example of the correlation between ice cream cones and shark attacks, and I said that those two things are correlated.
cues.zh: 當時舉了冰淇淋甜筒與鯊魚攻擊的有趣例子，說兩者彼此相關。

cues.en: So when people eat more ice cream cones, there are more shark attacks, but that's not because of a direct relationship, it's because of an indirect relationship that's actually due to changes in the weather.
cues.zh: 人們多吃冰淇淋甜筒時，鯊魚攻擊也較多，但不是直接關係，而是天氣變化造成的間接關係。

cues.en: So let's imagine this is the weather.
cues.zh: 假設這是天氣。

cues.en: This is the sort of ambient temperature over the course of weeks or whatever and this will be ice cream and this will be shark attack.
cues.zh: 例如數週內的環境溫度，這邊是冰淇淋，這邊是鯊魚攻擊。

cues.en: So the weather is correlated with eating ice cream and weather is also correlated with shark attacks.
cues.zh: 天氣與吃冰淇淋相關，也與鯊魚攻擊相關。

cues.en: But because people are going to the beach more often, so 2 and 3 here eating ice cream, and the number of shark attacks appear to be correlated,
cues.zh: 因為人們更常去海邊，所以這裡的 2 與 3，也就是吃冰淇淋與鯊魚攻擊次數，看起來相關，

cues.en: but that's not a true direct correlation.
cues.zh: 但那不是真正的直接相關。

cues.en: It's actually driven by these other correlations in the data here.
cues.zh: 實際上，是由資料中其他這些相關驅動的。

cues.en: Okay, so that's the idea of why we want something like a partial correlation.
cues.zh: 這就是我們需要偏相關這類方法的原因。

cues.en: We wanna know what is the correlation between ice cream cones consumed and shark attacks when partialing out effects attributable to the weather.
cues.zh: 我們想知道，排除可歸因於天氣的影響之後，冰淇淋甜筒消費量與鯊魚攻擊的相關是多少。

cues.en: Okay, so then we will get a system that looks like this, and these are the partial correlations.
cues.zh: 接著可能得到像這樣的系統，這些就是偏相關。

cues.en: This character here, it looks a little bit like an italics p, but in fact it's the Greek character rho, it's spelled R-H-O in Latin characters,
cues.zh: 這個字元有點像斜體 p，但其實是希臘字母 rho，用拉丁字母拼作 R-H-O，

cues.en: but it's the Greek character rho.
cues.zh: 它是希臘字母 rho。

cues.en: So we might get a result like this that when we partial out for variable 1, in fact, the correlation between ice cream consumption and shark attacks goes to 0
cues.zh: 可能得到這樣的結果：排除變數 1 後，冰淇淋消費量與鯊魚攻擊之間的相關，其實降為 0，

cues.en: because of this shared variance here.
cues.zh: 因為這裡有共同變異。

cues.en: Okay, so let me give you another example.
cues.zh: 再舉一個例子。

cues.en: Let's say we are doing a study on socioeconomic status, which I will call variable m for money.
cues.zh: 假設研究社經地位，用變數 m 表示，m 代表 money。

cues.en: And GMAT, if you're not familiar with the GMAT, is a standardized exam that is used to get into business school.
cues.zh: 以及 GMAT。如果你不熟悉，GMAT 是申請商學院使用的標準化測驗。

cues.en: So if you want to go to business school, you're gonna have to take a GMAT.
cues.zh: 想進商學院，就得考 GMAT。

cues.en: I'll call that variable g.
cues.zh: 把它稱為變數 g。

cues.en: And the hours spent studying for the GMAT, I'll call that s for study hours.
cues.zh: 準備 GMAT 所花的讀書時數，則稱為 s，代表 study hours。

cues.en: So we want to know if socioeconomic status is related to GMAT when partialing out hours spent studying.
cues.zh: 我們想知道，排除讀書時數後，社經地位是否與 GMAT 有關。

cues.en: So basically the question is: Are rich kids getting into business school because they get higher GMAT scores, regardless of how much time they spent studying?
cues.zh: 基本問題是：不論花多少時間讀書，有錢人家的孩子是否因為 GMAT 分數較高，而得以進入商學院？

cues.en: Okay, now just as a warning, I'm making up all these data like I make up all the data in this course.
cues.zh: 先提醒一下，這些資料都是我編的，就像課程中所有資料一樣。

cues.en: So these are not real numbers, I'm just kind of imagining this stuff.
cues.zh: 這些不是真實數字，只是想像出來的。

cues.en: All right, so here are the three raw correlation coefficients between these three variables.
cues.zh: 這是三個變數之間的三個原始相關係數。

cues.en: So these are not the partial correlations, these are just the raw correlations.
cues.zh: 不是偏相關，只是原始相關。

cues.en: So let's say that we find in our dataset the correlation between socioeconomic status and GMAT performance is .7.
cues.zh: 假設在資料集中，發現社經地位與 GMAT 表現的相關是 0.7。

cues.en: If this were a real number, if we really found this number in real data, that would be a little bit terrifying because it would basically mean that rich kids get a huge boost
cues.zh: 如果這是真實資料中真的發現的數字，就會有點可怕，因為那基本上表示有錢人家的孩子，

cues.en: for getting into business school just because of their socioeconomic status.
cues.zh: 只憑社經地位，就在進商學院時有很大優勢。

cues.en: But we look at the other variables in these datasets, and then we see it's actually difficult to interpret just this raw correlation because of the other correlations
cues.zh: 但查看資料集中的其他變數後，會發現因為資料集中還有其他相關，

cues.en: that we see in this dataset as well.
cues.zh: 所以單看這個原始相關，其實很難解讀。

cues.en: So that's why I'm now going to compute some partial correlations.
cues.zh: 因此，接著計算一些偏相關。

cues.en: So those are written like this.
cues.zh: 寫法如下。

cues.en: So we have the partial correlation of socioeconomic status with GMAT scores when partialing out
cues.zh: 這是社經地位與 GMAT 成績之間的偏相關，同時排除，

cues.en: or when controlling for the time spent studying on the GMAT.
cues.zh: 也就是控制準備 GMAT 的讀書時間。

cues.en: And here, the partial correlation actually goes down to 0.
cues.zh: 這裡的偏相關實際上降為 0。

cues.en: It's a pretty dramatic decrease from .7 to 0.
cues.zh: 從 0.7 降到 0，幅度相當大。

cues.en: So this partial correlation actually tells us that there is no trivial relationship between socioeconomic status and GMAT exam scores
cues.zh: 這個偏相關其實告訴我們，社經地位與 GMAT 考試分數之間沒有明顯的關係，

cues.en: when we remove the shared variance due to time spent studying.
cues.zh: 只要移除讀書時間造成的共同變異。

cues.en: So basically, what these mean, what these partial correlations mean is that people from higher socioeconomic status spend more time studying, and that's why they get higher scores on the GMAT.
cues.zh: 基本上，這些偏相關表示，社經地位較高的人花更多時間讀書，因此 GMAT 分數較高。

cues.en: And it's not just because they come from families with more money.
cues.zh: 而不是單純因為他們來自比較有錢的家庭。

cues.en: Again, I'm making up these data.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，這些資料是我編的。

cues.en: So this just sort of...
cues.zh: 這只是某種……

cues.en: This is like a result that I would kind of like to happen in the real world.
cues.zh: 我會希望真實世界出現的結果。

cues.en: And here, so here, I wrote NA for not applicable.
cues.zh: 這裡寫 NA，表示不適用。

cues.en: This is the correlation between socioeconomic status and the time spent studying when partialing out the GMAT exam.
cues.zh: 這是排除 GMAT 考試之後，社經地位與讀書時間之間的相關。

cues.en: Now, technically, you can compute this, but it's kind of weird to interpret this partial correlation.
cues.zh: 技術上可以計算，但這個偏相關的解讀有點奇怪。

cues.en: And so it doesn't really make sense in the context of the research question here.
cues.zh: 在這裡的研究問題脈絡中，不太有意義。

cues.en: So that's why I wrote NA, I didn't even bother computing it.
cues.zh: 因此寫 NA，甚至沒有費事去算。

cues.en: So this highlights a difference between kind of pure mathematics and applied mathematics, particularly in statistics.
cues.zh: 這凸顯了純數學與應用數學之間的差別，尤其在統計學中。

cues.en: So you'll often find situations where there are things that are possible to compute, they're mathematically possible to compute, you can implement them in computer code,
cues.zh: 你常會遇到某些東西，數學上能計算，也能實作成程式碼，

cues.en: and plug some numbers and get an answer, but that doesn't necessarily mean that it's going to be a sensible answer that is useful for addressing the research question at hand.
cues.zh: 代入數字得到答案，但不代表答案合理，或有助於回答眼前的研究問題。

cues.en: So just something to keep in mind.
cues.zh: 這一點要記得。

cues.en: The realm of possibilities of analyses is much greater than the realm of sensible, meaningful, interpretable analyses.
cues.zh: 可能進行的分析範圍，遠大於合理、有意義、可解讀的分析範圍。

cues.en: Okay, so now, I've explained a bit about partial correlations, gave some motivations.
cues.zh: 我已經稍微說明偏相關，也介紹了一些動機。

cues.en: Here was an example.
cues.zh: 這裡是一個例子。

cues.en: And now, I'm sure you're wondering, "How exactly does this work?
cues.zh: 現在你一定在想：「它究竟如何運作？

cues.en: This seems magical to compute a partial correlation."
cues.zh: 計算偏相關，看起來好神奇。」

cues.en: So it's not magic, it is math.
cues.zh: 這不是魔法，而是數學。

cues.en: Here is the formula for the partial correlation.
cues.zh: 這是偏相關的公式。

cues.en: This is the partial correlation between x and y when accounting for any shared variance with z.
cues.zh: 表示將與 Z 的任何共同變異納入考量後，X 與 Y 之間的偏相關。

cues.en: This is sort of obtuse-looking formula.
cues.zh: 這個公式看起來有點難懂。

cues.en: I actually do not recommend memorizing this formula.
cues.zh: 其實我不建議背下來。

cues.en: This is not a formula that you should spend brain energy committing to memory.
cues.zh: 這不是值得花腦力記憶的公式。

cues.en: In fact, I don't have this formula.
cues.zh: 事實上，我自己也沒記住。

cues.en: I had to look it up for this slide.
cues.zh: 為了這張投影片，我還得去查。

cues.en: But there are a couple of things, two things in particular that I want to point out, so that they are conceptually clear about how partial correlations work.
cues.zh: 但有幾點，特別是兩點，我想指出，讓你從概念上理解偏相關如何運作。

cues.en: The first point is to just look at the numerator here and see that the numerator is the correlation that we're interested in, the raw correlation between x and y.
cues.zh: 首先看分子，它是我們感興趣的相關，也就是 X 與 Y 的原始相關。

cues.en: And then what we subtract off is the product of the correlations between each individual variable and the variable that we are not interested in or that we are partialing out.
cues.zh: 接著減掉的，是各個變數與我們不感興趣，也就是要排除的變數之間的相關，相乘的結果。

cues.en: We wanna remove this variance attributable to anything having to do with z.
cues.zh: 我們要移除任何可歸因於 Z 的變異。

cues.en: So rxy minus rxz times ryz.
cues.zh: 也就是 rxy 減 rxz 乘 ryz。

cues.en: So we're subtracting off that variance and then we have these normalization terms in the denominator.
cues.zh: 我們減去那個變異，分母則有這些正規化項。

cues.en: Okay, so that's one thing I want to point out, that the numerator involves the thing that we're interested in minus the things that we are not interested in.
cues.zh: 這是我想指出的一點：分子包含我們感興趣的東西，減去不感興趣的東西。

cues.en: And then I would also like to do a quick thought experiment of what happens when there is nothing to partial out.
cues.zh: 另外也想快速做個思想實驗：如果沒有任何東西需要排除，會發生什麼事？

cues.en: So when there's no correlation between x and z, I should say zero correlation, and zero correlation between y and z.
cues.zh: 也就是 X 與 Z 沒有相關，應該說零相關，而且 Y 與 Z 也零相關。

cues.en: So let's think about what that's going to do with this formula.
cues.zh: 想想這會讓公式變成什麼樣子。

cues.en: So in the correlation between x and z and between y and z are zero, this obviously goes to zero.
cues.zh: X 與 Z，以及 Y 與 Z 的相關都為 0 時，這裡顯然變成 0。

cues.en: This here, r squared, is zero, this is zero, so we end up with the square root of one, which is one times the square root of one, which is also one.
cues.zh: 這裡 r 平方是 0，這裡也是 0，所以得到 1 的平方根，也就是 1，再乘上另一個 1 的平方根，也是 1。

cues.en: So basically, all this stuff cancels out.
cues.zh: 基本上，這些部分全都消掉。

cues.en: So when the partial correlation between x and y accounting for the common variance with z is computed and there's is actually no shared variance with z,
cues.zh: 所以，計算 X 與 Y 的偏相關，考慮它們與 Z 的共同變異時，如果其實與 Z 沒有共同變異，

cues.en: then the partial correlation reduces to the simple correlation between x and ys.
cues.zh: 偏相關就簡化成 X 與 Y 的一般相關。

cues.en: That's another thing I would like you to keep in mind about this formula.
cues.zh: 這是這個公式另一個希望你記住的地方。

cues.en: Now, in this video, I'm only explaining or showing examples of partial correlations with respect to one variable.
cues.zh: 這支影片只說明或示範排除一個變數的偏相關。

cues.en: It's possible to partial out with respect to multiple variables.
cues.zh: 也可以排除多個變數。

cues.en: So we can say rho xy, partialing out z, comma w, comma u, comma v.
cues.zh: 例如 rho xy，同時排除 z、w、u、v。

cues.en: You can have a bunch of other variables here.
cues.zh: 這裡可以有很多其他變數。

cues.en: And this formula is going to look kind of similar, except you're just gonna be subtracting more terms.
cues.zh: 公式看起來會類似，只是要減去更多項。

cues.en: So you also have to subtract out rxw and ryw, and you also have to normalize by one minus r squared,
cues.zh: 也要減去 rxw 與 ryw，並且用 1 減 r 平方來正規化，

cues.en: rxw and yw.
cues.zh: 也就是 rxw 與 ryw。

cues.en: So the formula gets a little bit longer, but it's possible to extend this for multiple variables.
cues.zh: 所以公式會長一些，但可以延伸到多個變數。

cues.en: So in this video, you learned about partial correlations, what they are, how to interpret them, and I showed you the formula to compute the partial correlation.
cues.zh: 這支影片學到偏相關是什麼、如何解讀，也看到了計算偏相關的公式。

cues.en: In the next video, you'll see how this gets implemented in code.
cues.zh: 下一支影片會看到如何用程式碼實作。
